title: Kiondo basket weaving
summary: The kiondo is a bag of hand-twisted plant twine, most often sisal, finished with a leather strap, made by Kikuyu, Kamba and Taita women in Kenya. It is twined rather than coiled: pairs of strands twist round each other row after row, and bands of dyed twine make stripes and diamonds.
howToPlay: The lit case above the bench shows the kiondo as it should finish. Look at how its pattern climbs the curve.
Choose a strand colour below the basket, then lay each stitch across the front of the ring. The gold ring marks the next place and the strip under the basket shows the row in hand.
Work up from the base, one ring at a time, so each ring lines up with the bands in the case.
Press Check when every stitch is laid. Undo takes the last stitch back.
rules: The bag is built from 9 rings of 13 stitches, laid from the base upward, one ring at a time. The leather strap is already fitted.
Each stitch takes one of four twine colours: natural sisal, indigo, red or gold.
The score is the share of stitches whose colour matches the pattern, counted beyond what laying only the commonest colour would earn. Three stars need 88, two need 65 and one needs 40.
Undo takes back the last stitch. A bag left plain earns no stars.
heritageNote: Kiondo are made by women of the Kikuyu, Kamba and Taita communities, who spin the twine by hand, dye part of it, and twine it into the bag before adding leather trim. Women's groups sell them in markets today, and the colour bands often follow family or regional tastes.
